status: COLLECTED AND WRITTEN 2026-09-22. Counts in the article were computed by hand from data/consensus/west-african.json because build-evidence.mjs was not run in this pass. Re-run the pipeline and check the figures against the article before this page is treated as verified.
note: Method lives in .claude/skills/consensus-guide/SKILL.md. Read theScopeQuestion FIRST - it is the decision the whole guide rests on, and on this topic it is the difference between a West African guide and an African one. Then theStreetFoodProblem, then theSourceMixVerdict.
theScopeQuestion:
RULING: WEST AFRICA ONLY, WITH THE NATIONAL CUISINE AS THE FACET AXIS. Nigeria, Ghana, Senegal, The Gambia, Sierra Leone and Ivory Coast are the six that the sources actually fill; Cameroon appears inside menus rather than as a restaurant of its own.

WHY IT IS NOT AN 'AFRICAN' GUIDE, and this is settled by what the serious sources publish rather than by preference:
  Time Out        '17 Best Nigerian and West African Restaurants in London', by Joyce Oladeinde, a British Nigerian food writer. Not one Ethiopian or Moroccan restaurant on it.
  The Infatuation TWO separate guides on one domain - 'Where To Eat West African Food In London' and 'Where To Eat Nigerian Food In London', both by Riaz Phillips.
  Olive           'West African restaurants in London: Toyo Odetunde shares her favourite insider spots'.
  The Handbook    '8 Of The Best West African Restaurants In London'.
  Michelin        classifies Akoko, Chishuru and Ikoyi as 'West African' in the starred list, not as 'African'.
FOUR OF THE FIVE STRONGEST SOURCES IN THE TOPIC PUT 'WEST AFRICAN' IN THE TITLE. The generalist 'African restaurants in London' lists - London x London's 18, London Kensington Guide's 28 - are the ones that sweep Ethiopian, Moroccan, Congolese and South African into one heading, and they are the weaker pages.

HOW THE AFRICAN-WIDE LISTS WERE SCOPED. Every name on them was assigned a cuisine and dropped if it was not West African. Full list of drops is in data/consensus/west-african.json under outOfScopeDropped. The Infatuation makes the call for us on the hardest one: it includes Deluxe Manna in Tottenham and says in the entry itself, 'a Congolese spot, so not technically West African'. Dropped.

DO NOT REVISIT WITHOUT NEW EVIDENCE. The test to re-run: does a masthead publish a standalone 'best African restaurants in London' list that a West African reader would be served instead of a West African one? On 2026-09-22 the head-term SERP returned Time Out's and The Infatuation's WEST AFRICAN guides in the top three.
theNationalCuisineAxis:
USE THE COUNTRY, NOT 'AFRICAN', AND NOT AREA. Every strong source already does. Time Out's own standfirst promises 'food from Ghana, The Gambia and Ivory Coast'; The Infatuation's scope line is 'Senegal, Gambia, Ghana, or Nigeria'; Olive's writer labels Senegambian, Ivorian and Ghanaian separately and explains why the labels matter.

IT IS ALSO THE ONLY AXIS A READER CAN ACT ON. Nigerian and Ghanaian kitchens both sell jollof and both sell plantain, and nothing on a shopfront tells you which tradition you are walking into. Waakye is Ghanaian and you will not find it in a Nigerian dining room; abula is Yoruba and you will not find it in a Ghanaian one.

WHY NOT AREA: because the geography is a consequence of the cuisine, not an alternative to it. Peckham and the Old Kent Road are Nigerian; Tottenham and Plaistow are Ghanaian; the Senegambian kitchens are scattered (Southwark, Elephant and Castle, Islington, Walworth); the one Ivorian restaurant is in Brockley. Area becomes a cross-reference table at the top of the page, which is where it belongs.
theStreetFoodProblem:
MARKET STALLS AND TAKEAWAY COUNTERS ARE CENTRAL, NOT A FOOTNOTE, AND THE SOURCES SETTLED IT.

THE SCENE'S BEST-KNOWN KITCHENS STARTED ON STALLS. Chishuru holds a Michelin star and began as a three-month pop-up in Brixton Village won in the Brixton Kitchen competition in 2019. The Flygerians started as street food and pop-ups and now trade out of Peckham Palms. Suuyar was a stall on the corner of Choumert Road and Rye Lane before it took a shop at the tip of Peckham Rye. Naija High Street is still a lunchtime stall in Lower Marsh Market and The Infatuation lists it beside two Michelin-starred restaurants.

THE INFATUATION PRINTS THE FORMAT PER VENUE and roughly half its West African list is takeaway-led: 'Serious Takeout Operation' is tagged on Waakye Joint, Bola Cuisine, Angels Bakery, Aso Rock, Alhaji Suya, Naija High Street, Eko Bar, Chuku's and 805.

NAMED TRADERS ONLY. Peckham Palms, Peckham Levels, Rye Lane Market, Lower Marsh Market, Borough Yards and The Africa Centre are buildings, not venues, and several are already recorded in markets.json and street-food.json. Record the trader. See outOfScopeDropped in the consensus file.

PECKHAM IS THE CENTRE AND THE EVIDENCE IS SPECIFIC. Choumert Road alone holds Lolak Afrique (38-40), Mingles (18) and, until it moved, the Suuyar stall on the Rye Lane corner. Alhaji Suya is on Peckham Park Road, The Flygerians in Peckham Palms on Bournemouth Close, Wazobia and KayBizz Dishes elsewhere in SE15. BRIXTON gives Enish on Coldharbour Lane, Sato's Kitchen, an Alhaji Suya branch and Asafo up on Brixton Hill - and it is where Chishuru began. DEPTFORD IS THE ONE THE FOOD GUIDES MISS: it has no West African restaurant that any source in this pass names, but it has Akwaba Market, the Ivorian grocery whose owners went on to open Sikatiô in Brockley.

awardBodies.name: Michelin Guide
awardBodies.verified: 2026-09-22 - READ DIRECTLY FROM THE AWARDING BODY, STARS AND BIB GOURMAND BOTH.
awardBodies.note:
READ THIS BEFORE ANY FUTURE PASS TOUCHES MICHELIN. data/sources.json lists guide.michelin.com under blocked.permanent403 with a stars-only Wikipedia substitute. THAT ENTRY IS WRONG. The site answers plain `curl -sL --max-time 45 <url>` with HTTP 200 and full HTML. What triggers the HTTP 202 empty body is sending a browser user agent - passing -A with a Chrome string is what made every previous pass believe it was blocked. Fetch with NO user agent at all. List pages paginate as /page/2, /page/3.

THE CUISINE FILTER IS THE FAST ROUTE: /gb/en/greater-london/london/restaurants/african. It prints '3 restaurants' and that is the whole Greater London African selection.

2026 MICHELIN GUIDE UNITED KINGDOM, GREATER LONDON, AFRICAN:
  Chishuru  One Star: High quality cooking. Cuisine African. ££££. /restaurant/chishuru
  Akoko     One Star: High quality cooking. Cuisine African. /restaurant/akoko
  Akara     Bib Gourmand: good quality, good value cooking. Cuisine African, Brazilian. ££. /restaurant/akara
ALL THREE HOLD A DISTINCTION AND TWO OF THEM SHARE AN OWNER, Aji Akokomi. That is a finding, not a coincidence, and it is the spine of the guide's first section.

TRAP 15 CHECKED on the filter page: it also links MRBL, Bar des Pres Mayfair and AO by Daniel Rogan. Those are the 'you might also like' rail, not results - AO is in Southampton, which gives it away.

IKOYI IS NOT IN THE AFRICAN SELECTION. Its own Michelin page reads 'Two Stars: Excellent cooking restaurant in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide United Kingdom' with Cuisine: CREATIVE. The Wikipedia starred list labels it West African; the awarding body does not. Its two stars are a real dated fact and are printed; Michelin is not counted as a West African citation for it. See openVenueQuestions.

THE BIB GOURMAND QUESTION IS NOW SETTLED. London x London's 'It took a Bib Gourmand in the 2026 guide' is correct. London Best Eats' 'Michelin Guide: Good Cooking' label is not.

awardBodies.name: National Restaurant Awards
awardBodies.note:
Voted by an academy of more than 200 chefs, restaurateurs and food writers across 11 UK regions; the method is published at /how-the-list-is-created/. UK-WIDE (trap 12) but the town prints beside every name, so the London subset is readable.

2026 LIST (live on the site, and already up on 9 June 2026): Ikoyi #24, Chishuru #77. No Akoko. The Ritz and Osip are tied at #2, so 100 restaurants carry 99 ranks - that is the awards' own tie, not an extraction error.
2025 LIST (Wayback, 5 December 2025): Ikoyi #16, Chishuru #40, Akoko #52.
2024 SPECIAL AWARDS (Wayback, 30 July 2024): Chef of the Year, Adejoké Bakare (Chishuru). Chef to Watch, Ayo Adeyemi (then head chef at Akoko).
2026 SPECIAL AWARDS: Trailblazer of the Year, Maria Bradford - a Sierra Leonean chef, but her restaurant Shwen Shwen is in Sevenoaks, Kent. Not London. Not counted.

THE ARCHIVE IS THE ONLY ROUTE TO PAST YEARS. The site rebuilds each cycle and keeps no results archive of its own; web.archive.org's CDX index has captures of /list/Awards for 2024 but none for 2025.

awardBodies.name: The Good Food Guide
awardBodies.note:
HAS A 'WEST AFRICAN' CUISINE FILTER, which is the fastest way in: POST or GET /search with cuisine[352]. The results render client-side and come back empty to curl, so read the sitemap instead - https://www.thegoodfoodguide.co.uk/sitemap-auto.xml lists every /restaurant/<slug>/id/<n> page.

LONDON WEST AFRICAN ENTRIES: Akoko (44732), Chishuru (61372), Akara (61872), Chuku's (42532), Ikoyi (33032). The scoring band (Good / Very Good / Exceptional / World Class / Local Gem) sits behind the membership paywall and was not recorded.

DATED AWARD: Chuku's is named in Best Local Restaurants in London 2025, published 15 July 2025. Ida in Queen's Park was the London winner.

TRAP 12: Britain's 100 Best Local Restaurants 2026 is national. Its only West African entry in the readable half is Shwen Shwen at #40, Sevenoaks, Kent. Ranks 51-100 are paywalled and were not read.

awardBodies.name: The World's 50 Best Restaurants
awardBodies.note: Ikoyi, No. 15 in the 2025 list and winner of the Highest Climber Award 2025, sponsored by Lee Kum Kee. Worth reading for the scope question as much as the rank: the list's own write-up calls the cooking 'category-free cuisine' and says Chan's style 'defies categorisation'.

awardBodiesChecked: THERE IS NO WEST AFRICAN FOOD AWARD IN BRITAIN that this pass could find, which is the opposite of the Caribbean topic, where the award exists and its website is dead. Here the mainstream awards do the work instead, and unusually well: three London West African restaurants hold Michelin stars, two are in the National Restaurant Awards hundred, one is 15th in the world. This is the most award-covered cuisine guide on the site after the Michelin-heavy generalist ones.

UK Caribbean Food Awards - has a 'Best African Eatery' category. NOT a West African award and out of scope for this topic; noted because the Caribbean config already records the body and someone will find it.
African Restaurant Week / Best of Africa style awards - not checked in this pass. Worth ten minutes before the next one.
Harden's (hardens.com, tier A) - has no African or West African cuisine index; /uk-london/cuisine-african/ 404s.
Estrella Damm Top 50 Gastropubs, National Pizza Awards and the rest of the register's tier A are irrelevant here.

editorialLists.name: Time Out
editorialLists.note: 17 venues, Joyce Oladeinde, 30 June 2026. THE BROADEST LIST IN THE TOPIC and the byline is why - a British Nigerian food writer, not a generalist, and she attributes a country to most entries. NOT RANKED despite the 1-17 numbering: the standfirst presents a selection and Little Baobab sits at #2 above two starred restaurants. Do not record a rank.

editorialLists.name: The Infatuation
editorialLists.note: TWO GUIDES, ONE DOMAIN, ONE SOURCE. The West African guide (14 entries, 9 October 2024) and the Nigerian guide (13 entries, 23 December 2024) are both by Riaz Phillips - the same writer whose Eater map anchors the Caribbean corpus, which is worth knowing if the two topics are ever compared. Trap 16 checked: the name arrays differ, so this is not one page recorded twice. Ratings are published per venue but page order is not rating order, so no rank is recorded. It is also the only source that prints the FORMAT per venue - 'Serious Takeout Operation', 'Cheap Eats', 'Halal' - which is what makes the street-food section buildable.

editorialLists.name: Olive Magazine
editorialLists.note: 14 venues, Toyo Odetunde, 10 July 2026, updated 11 August 2026. THE MOST USEFUL SOURCE FOR THE NATIONAL AXIS. It is the only list that reaches Senegambian cooking with more than one address (Safna Kitchen, Walfathou Kitchen, Little Baobab) and the only one naming Kneluchii in Beckenham. It flags its own out-of-London entry - 'Though it is outside London (in Sevenoaks)' for Shwen Shwen - which is trap 12 handled by the source itself.

editorialLists.name: The Handbook
editorialLists.note: 8 venues, Patrick Dunne, dated 16 February 2026 although the title still says 'The 2024 List'. Thin, but it is the only tier-B source naming Stork in Mayfair, and its Sikatiô entry is where the Vittles connection surfaced.

editorialLists.name: Secret London
editorialLists.note: 10 venues, Vaishnavi Pandey, 15 August 2024. COUNT THE SOURCE, DO NOT USE ITS FACTS - it gives Chishuru's address as 9 Market Row, Brixton, which the restaurant left in 2022, and says Akoko 'recently reopened with a new head chef, Theo Clench', which nothing else supports. It is in because it is registered tier C and because it is the only source naming Eazy Kitchen in Walworth.

editorialLists.name: London x London
editorialLists.note: 18 African venues, Lauren Kendrick, 27 August 2022, updated 12 September 2026. Ten survive the West African scope. Its Chishuru entry is still the Brixton one, so the update was partial. Only source for Wazobia, Presidential Suya and Asafo. Its Akara entry carries the unverified Bib Gourmand claim - see the Michelin note.

editorialLists.name: Vittles
editorialLists.note: NEW DOMAIN, NOT IN data/sources.json. Jonathan Nunn's Vittles is the most serious independent London food publication going, and it is the only source in this pass that reviews West African places at length rather than listing them. The Vittles 99 (December 2025) is a genuinely ranked list of 99 London restaurants; ranks 99-87, 75-69, 40-33 and 10-8 are readable free, the rest is paywalled. Sikatiô is #34 and Ikoyi #10. Its two full reviews - Sikatiô (November 2023) and 'A Tale of Two Suya Shops' (May 2025) - are where the suya scene gets documented at all. Archive is searchable through Substack's API at /api/v1/archive?sort=new&search=<term>.

assessedAndExcluded.verdict: EXCLUDE - TRAP 2 SYNDICATION. '18 Best Nigerian and West African Restaurants in London' is Time Out's article reproduced verbatim, 'Time Out tip' lines intact, posted under 'Submitted by daniel' on 22 January 2026. Time Out is the source.

EXCLUDE ITS WEST AFRICAN PAGE - AND IT IS REGISTERED TIER C, SO THIS NEEDS A HUMAN CALL. /cuisine/west-african is generated by a cuisine filter, not written: five venues, each with an aggregated star score (4.8, 4.6, 4.5), a price band and a one-line 'At its core:' summary. A filterable database is not an opinion, the same call made on blackeatsldn.com in caribbean.json and dinehalal.uk in halal.json.
assessedAndExcluded.butKeepThisName: It is the only place this pass found SPINACH & AGUSHI in Exmouth Market, a Ghanaian counter. No countable source names it. A later pass should look for one.

assessedAndExcluded.verdict: EXCLUDE - SEO CONTENT FARM. '28 Best African Restaurants in London (Nigerian, Ethiopian, Ghanaian, Moroccan & More)'. Title assembled from keywords, US spellings throughout on a London site ('cozy', 'colorful', 'flavorful'), no evidence of a visit in 28 entries, 'ALSO SEE:' keyword links threaded through the list, byline 'Bianca' with no bio. Fails the data/serp/README test on three named tells. Not currently in data/sources.json; belongs in `excluded`.

EXCLUDE ITS AFRICAN VIDEO - AND IT IS REGISTERED TIER D, SO THIS NEEDS A HUMAN CALL. 'Top 10 Best African Restaurants in London' carries the disclaimer 'We have used video footage and images to maximize the clarity of the content ... Footage, music, image, and graphics used in the video belong to their respective owners.' No visit, no named creator, stock music, 356 views. The video tier's version of a content farm.

NOT SEEDABLE AS A LIST. 'I visited London's only Senegalese restaurant and it felt like an...' is a single-venue review from a real Reach masthead. Single-venue features are not a list and cannot be recorded as one - the same call the Caribbean pass made on The Voice.
EXCLUDE. 'Top 20 Senegalese Restaurants In London' is a directory listing page. No byline, no visit.
EXCLUDE - already excluded globally. Ranked second on the head-term SERP.

excludeOnSight: akoko.co.uk, chishuru.com, akaralondon.co.uk, chukuslondon.co.uk, 805restaurants.com, enish.co.uk, 19fiftyseven.co.uk, theflygerians.com, littlebaobab.co.uk, pitangalondon.com, asorockfood.com, papisgrill.co.uk, alhajisuya.com - venues' own sites. Tier F, weight 0, used for addresses, prices and booking links only.
thefork.co.uk, opentable.co.uk, yelp.com - booking and review platforms, already excluded.
theSourceMixVerdict:
THE TOPIC IS STRONGLY SOURCED AND THE FLOOR IS MET. FIFTEEN distinct domains across FOUR tiers: four tier A (Michelin, the National Restaurant Awards, The Good Food Guide, The World's 50 Best), four tier B mastheads, three tier C independents and four tier D YouTube creators. One hundred and fifteen citations across forty-three venues, twenty-four of them named by two or more independent domains.

TIER D IS THE PART THAT CHANGED THE RESULT, exactly as SKILL.md predicts. Nine of the forty-three venues reach this guide only through YouTube: Mingles, Gold Coast, Sato's Kitchen, KayBizz Dishes, Suuyar (with Vittles), Papi's Grill (with Time Out), Naija High Street (with The Infatuation), Pitanga and Stork. Two of the four creators are Nigerian-food channels documenting kitchens no masthead has written up. Social is four of fifteen voices, 27%, well under the 70% flag.

TIER E IS EMPTY AND THAT IS THE ONE REAL HOLE. Reddit is blocked to curl and to the browser in this environment. A judged award exists, so scripts/audit-source-mix.mjs wants two social voices rather than three and tier D already carries four - the floor passes on the count. It does not pass on the spirit: there is no community voice in this corpus at all.

THE SHAPE RISK NO SCRIPT CATCHES. The top of the ranking is decided by the fine-dining end, because that is where the awards are. Akoko, Chishuru and Ikoyi are named by nine or ten domains each; Aso Rock, Kate's Cafe and Bola Cuisine - three of the kitchens the community actually eats in - are named by two, one and one. The article is structured so the counts do not bury them: the national-cuisine sections, the cheapest section and the street-food section are all places where a two-source venue leads.

facetAxis.note: The country a kitchen cooks from. Use the operator's own description where there is one; the lists disagree on labels more than the restaurants do.

values.label: Nigerian
values.describeAs: jollof rice cooked down until the bottom of the pot smokes, egusi - a stew thickened with ground melon seed - and suya, thin beef grilled and dusted in yaji, a peanut and chilli spice mix

values.label: Ghanaian
values.describeAs: waakye, rice and black-eyed beans steamed with dried sorghum leaves until both turn red-brown, served with fish, egg, gari and shito; plus banku and kenkey, the fermented corn doughs eaten with soup

values.label: Ivorian
values.describeAs: grilled or deep-fried tilapia and croaker with attiéké, a fluffy cassava couscous, and sauce arachide, a peanut stew

values.label: Senegalese and Gambian
values.describeAs: thieboudienne, the fish-and-rice dish jollof descends from; yassa, chicken or fish under caramelised onion and lime; and mafé or domoda, a peanut stew

values.label: Sierra Leonean
values.describeAs: plasas, cassava leaf pounded and cooked down with palm oil and fish or meat, eaten with rice

values.label: Pan-West African and fine dining
values.describeAs: tasting-menu kitchens that cook across the region rather than from one country

facetAxis.checkBeforePrinting: SIERRA LEONEAN IS THE THIN ONE. Exactly one London venue in this corpus is Sierra Leonean - Mingles on Choumert Road, named by one YouTube channel. The best-known Sierra Leonean kitchen in Britain, Maria Bradford's Shwen Shwen, is in Sevenoaks and is not London. IVORIAN rests entirely on Sikatiô, but that venue is named by four domains including a #34 place in the Vittles 99, so the section stands on one address honestly. SENEGALESE has a live problem: Little Baobab is the only dedicated Senegalese restaurant four sources name and Time Out marked it temporarily closed in September 2026 - see openVenueQuestions.

formatSection.title: Market stalls and counters
formatSection.note: THE SECTION THE PUBLISHED LISTS TREAT AS A FOOTNOTE AND THIS SCENE TREATS AS THE MAIN ROUTE. Named traders only. Several of the best-known West African kitchens in London started on a stall and two of them still are one, which is the story worth telling rather than a list of halls. The verified stall-to-restaurant lines: Chishuru (Brixton Kitchen competition 2019 -> three-month Brixton Village pop-up -> Fitzrovia -> Michelin star, 5 February 2024); The Flygerians (street food and pop-ups from 2016 -> Peckham Palms); Suuyar (stall on the Choumert Road and Rye Lane corner -> a shop at the tip of Peckham Rye). Still stalls: Naija High Street in Lower Marsh Market, Waterloo; D&K Gambian Roast Chicken and Rice in Forest Gate Market.

knownGaps: TIER E IS EMPTY. Reddit is blocked to curl and to the browser in this environment, so no community thread is recorded. Only fix is Rob pasting thread URLs by hand. This is the single weakest thing about the corpus and it is invisible in the counts, because tier D over-delivered.

RESOLVED 2026-09-22, AND IT IS NOT A GAP ANY MORE - BUT data/sources.json STILL SAYS IT IS. guide.michelin.com is readable with plain curl and no user agent; only a browser user agent gets the 202. The blocked.permanent403 entry and the stars-only Wikipedia substitute need removing centrally. Until they are, every topic on this site is still reading Michelin through a substitute that cannot show a Bib Gourmand - which is exactly the failure already recorded against the Vietnamese corpus in substituteCaveats, and it cost this topic Akara's Bib until a second pair of eyes caught it.

THE VITTLES 99 IS MOSTLY PAYWALLED. Ranks 99-87, 75-69, 40-33 and 10-8 are free; 86-76, 68-41, 32-11 and 7-1 are not. Sikatiô at #34 and Ikoyi at #10 are both in readable bands, but there may be West African entries in the bands this pass could not read, and the Vittles 99 is the only ranked London-wide list in the corpus.

THE GOOD FOOD GUIDE'S SCORING BANDS ARE PAYWALLED. The five London West African entries are confirmed as inspected entries; whether each is Good, Very Good, Exceptional or a Local Gem is not recorded, so no band is printed.

SEARCH IS BROKEN IN THIS ENVIRONMENT AND IT LIMITED THE BLOG TIER. Bing's RSS endpoint answers the first query of a session and then returns single-token junk for the rest; DuckDuckGo lite and html both serve a challenge; Mojeek returns an empty results page. One clean SERP was captured for the head term and everything after that was direct fetching and site-by-site archive search. The independent tier is three domains, which is thinner than the topic deserves.

SPINACH & AGUSHI in Exmouth Market, a Ghanaian counter, is named by no countable source - it surfaced only on londonbesteats.com, which this pass declined. It is left out of the guide rather than carried on an uncountable source.
NO WEST AFRICAN FOOD AWARD WAS FOUND IN BRITAIN. African Restaurant Week and similar were not checked. Ten minutes before the next pass.
Per SKILL.md and the no-weakness-lines rule, NONE of the above may appear in the article. It lives here.
openVenueQuestions:
IKOYI - THE BIGGEST JUDGEMENT CALL ON THE PAGE, AND FIVE INDEPENDENT THINGS NOW POINT THE SAME WAY. (1) THE AWARDING BODY ITSELF: Michelin's 2026 entry gives its cuisine as CREATIVE and leaves it out of the Greater London African selection, which is exactly three restaurants and does not include it. (2) Its own website describes 'spice-based cuisine around British micro-seasonality' and never says West African. (3) Time Out's own entry: 'It isn't quite a West African restaurant.' (4) The Infatuation's West African guide, by the specialist who wrote both its African guides, leaves it out entirely. (5) Vittles: Chan and Hassan-Odukale 'managed to kid themselves - or kid their PR - that they were opening a West African restaurant'. Only Wikipedia's starred list calls it West African, and Wikipedia is not the awarding body.

IT IS STILL IN THE GUIDE, in a section of its own, with all of that printed plainly - eight domains name it, it holds two stars in the 2026 guide, it is #24 in the National Restaurant Awards 2026 and #15 in the world, and a reader searching this term will look for it. Michelin is NOT counted as a West African citation for it, which is why its count is eight and not nine. If Rob wants it cut entirely, nothing else on the page moves.

LITTLE BAOBAB - TIME OUT MARKED IT TEMPORARILY CLOSED IN SEPTEMBER 2026 and the operator says the Africa Centre building is the reason. Four domains name it and it is the only dedicated Senegalese restaurant in the corpus. KEPT OUT OF THE RECOMMENDATIONS per the house rule that a place a listing marks closed, even temporarily, is treated as closed. The cost is real: it leaves the Senegalese strand resting on Gambian and Senegambian kitchens instead. ASK ROB whether it is trading again before the next pass.

TATALE - GONE FROM THE AFRICA CENTRE. London x London and London Kensington Guide both still list Akwasi Brenya-Mensa's Tatale as the Africa Centre restaurant. The Africa Centre's own site says the ground-floor restaurant has been operated by Little Baobab since 6 September 2024. Whether Tatale trades anywhere else now is unknown. Left out of the guide.
OBALENDE SUYA, PECKHAM - Vittles states plainly 'today, Obalende is closed'. Recorded so the next pass does not chase it.

SUYA ACADEMY - TRAP 12 RISK, LEFT OUT ON PURPOSE. It appears only as a photo caption in Vittles' suya piece ('Box-fresh suya with all the trimmings at Suya Academy'). The same piece says one strand of the research 'took me on a c2c train as far as estuary Essex (and therefore is functionally useless to this review)'. Suya Academy may well be the Essex one. No address was found. Recorded in the corpus as a name; deliberately not placed in London and not in the article.

PAPA L'S KITCHEN, 16-17 Jermyn Street - named by Time Out (June 2026) and by Ugo Arinzeh, with a pre-theatre deal and Wednesday-to-Saturday hours. Its own domain would not answer on 2026-09-22 and no other route confirmed it is trading. Carried in the corpus; given a short entry with no link. Worth a phone call.

STORK, 13-14 Cork Street - named by The Handbook and Ugo Arinzeh only, and pan-African rather than West African, with a menu The Handbook describes as Ghanaian and Nigerian led. Two sources, one of them video. Left out of the guide's entries; kept in the corpus.

ALHAJI SUYA - MULTI-SITE AND MATERIALLY CHANGED. The Infatuation names Peckham, Greenwich, Brixton and Walworth. Vittles reports that it 'burnt down and reopened without a live fire grill', which is the single fact a reader chasing suya needs and which no other source carries. Its alhajisuya.com is a nationwide delivery shop rather than the shop's own page, so do not link it as the restaurant.

SUUYAR - TWO FORMATS AT ONCE. Vittles describes the original street stall on the corner of Choumert Road and Rye Lane and a newer bricks-and-mortar site 'at the tip of Peckham Rye'; My Tasty Naija filmed the buffet with owner Kolawole Ajayi. Whether the stall still trades alongside the shop is not established.

805 RESTAURANTS - BRANCH COUNT DISAGREES ACROSS SOURCES. Time Out says Old Kent Road, Hyde Park, Peckham and Hendon; The Handbook says Hyde Park, Old Kent Road and Hendon; the group's own site also lists Reading, Accra and Abuja. Only the London branches are in scope. Chains handling per chains.json.

ENISH - BRANCH COUNT DISAGREES TOO. Time Out says eleven London locations, London x London says six. Neither was verified against the group's own site, which is organised by country rather than by branch. The article names branches rather than a count.

PAPI'S GRILL - New Cross is London, Dartford is Kent. The operator's own site reads 'Afro-Fusion Dining In Dartford & New Cross'. Only the New Cross site is in scope; do not let the Dartford one inherit the citation.
KNELUCHII is in Beckenham and ROTI-style outer-London venues generally: Beckenham, Plumstead, Streatham and Tottenham are all Greater London and stay in. Sevenoaks and Dartford are not.

AKOKO'S HEAD CHEF HAS CHANGED TWICE. William Chilila to Ayo Adeyemi (February 2021) to Mutaro Baldé (September 2024), per Wikipedia. The star was won in 2024 under Adeyemi and retained under Baldé.
